design:
Decided with the operator on the mock, 2026-11-02. The mock is the shipped components fed fixtures, now on master: SpecPageHeader's compact design, SpecNotices, SpecListFooter, SpecDocList's marks (StateIcon) and the 'attention' order, SpecOpenPicker's marker, spec-notices.css and spec-list-marks.css. Building wires them to the Hub's data and removes every design not chosen.

Header (design B):
- Row 1: back/forward; in the panel a "Specs" switcher; the breadcrumb and slice arrows; then the notice count and the actions (Draft next, Check, the primary action, More, and in the panel the outline menu and close).
- Row 2: the title, the phase, the journey as four knots, kind, changed, the check result, and the health facts (requirements verified, drift, vault, tasks decided).
- The count shows how many notices the document has, in the tone of the most urgent, and opens them as a list: one line each, with its full text and its action on demand (e.g. an amendment's reason, how to check, Mark reviewed). Measured: 154px on the page whatever the messages.
- Every banner item becomes a notice or moves into the body: today's messages (unread errors, the deleted note, the phase controls' messages and refusals, approval gaps and notes, the blocking list), unreviewed and proposed amendments, retired requirements. Dialogs stay where they are. The journey-step and size control (exploring documents) moves into the notice list or the More menu, one click away.
- Condensed: once the body is scrolled, one line of 41px with the title, the phase, the count and the actions; clicking it, or scrolling back to the top, expands it.
- The side panel keeps today's four navigation rows (tabs, sections, requirement strip, Filter & sort): with the new header it measured 248 to 276px. A one-row version (134 to 162px) was mocked and declined.

Lists of specs, everywhere one is drawn (the Spec tab's column, the panel's Open a spec screen with its cards and All specs list, the panel's Specs switcher, the search dialog), since all of them are SpecDocList or SpecOpenPicker:
- Marks, set 2 "paperwork": writing a page with a pen, ready a paper plane, approved a green stamp, building the hammer, done a solid green disc with a check, capability a library, archived a faded box (and its title faded). The cards' status line uses the same marks.
- Defects by step starts folded, showing its count (Spec tab only; the pickers have no footer).
- Roadmap order lists every slice under the roadmap it names, in the roadmap's slice order.
- A fifth order, "What needs you": Waiting on you (each with its reason), In progress, Approved not started, Finished, Capabilities. Reasons: ready to approve (a document being written that the Hub's check finds nothing blocking), amendments to review (unreviewed or proposed), ready to build (approved, no build yet, open tasks), ready to fold (done, not folded). The pickers offer it in their order menu.

Declined on the mock: header A (one notice line, 190px), header C (cards in the right column), today's dot, a word per state, icon sets 1, 3 and 4.

problem:
Operator, 2026-10-28 (vault src-2a9cc1abc8e4) and 2026-11-02: on a 1920x1080 screen, in the side panel less than half of the height is the spec itself. On the spec page it looks fine until one error or warning shows, then the body drops below half, and it shrinks further with each warning. "I like a lot of stuff from the current design but there is too much that takes the screen." Also, 2026-11-02: opening a spec, the list's footer ("Defects by step") takes most of the spec list; the list does not group slices under their roadmap; and "the small green as done" does not show a spec is done. The operator asked that the list changes apply wherever specs are listed, including the side panel's first screen when searching for a spec.

Measured in the mock at 1920x1080 (real components, the operator's real amendment from "A finished spec gets a build retrospective"), from the top of the spec header to the first line of the body:
- Spec page: 290px with no message, 473px with one amendment, 667px with four messages (body 80%, 62%, 43% of the height).
- Side panel: 459px, 658px, 874px (body 57%, 38%, 17%).

Causes found in the code at f565d6d:
- SpecPageHeader.tsx has three rows (bar, title with actions, journey ribbon): 169px on the page, 198px in the panel.
- useSpecSurface's banner stacks every message, the health line and the full amendment card (about 185px) between the header and the body.
- SpecDefectsReport starts open (useState(true)) and lists every change with defects: 14 changes and 72 defects on the operator's project, about 500px of the list's column.
- The list groups a slice under its roadmap only through the spec index's `parent` (adapt.ts listEntries). 47 change documents name their roadmap in their own `roadmap` field and none has an index parent, so in the operator's app no slice is grouped. The list route does not return the `roadmap` field.
- spec-page.css draws approved and done as the same 7px green dot; done only adds a 1.5px inner ring. The same dot is drawn by SpecDocList's rows and by SpecOpenPicker's cards (This conversation, Building now, Recently opened); SpecOpenPicker is the panel's Open a spec screen, its Specs switcher and the Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K search dialog (SpecDocumentPicker).

requirements.rationale: Today it is 290 to 667px; the chosen design measured 154px.
requirements.statement: On the spec page in a 1920x1080 window with the header expanded, the first line of the document body starts at most 200px below the top of the spec header, whatever messages, warnings and facts are showing.

requirements.rationale: Today it is 459 to 874px; the chosen design measured 248 to 276px with the panel's four navigation rows kept.
requirements.statement: In the conversation's side panel in a 1920x1080 window, with the conversation column at its default 480px and the header expanded, the first line of the body starts at most 320px below the top of the spec header, the tabs and section navigation included, whatever messages are showing.

requirements.rationale: Each message adding its own height is what made the body shrink with every warning. The operator chose the count (B) over a line (A) and a side column (C).
requirements.statement: However many messages and warnings a document has, they add no height above the body: the header shows their count, in the tone of the most urgent, and the count opens all of them, each on one line with its full text and its action reachable from there.

Once the body is scrolled away from its top, the header condenses to a single line of at most 48px, in the page and in the panel, still showing the title, the phase, the message count, the primary action and the More menu; it expands again when the body returns to its top or the line is clicked.

Every action, navigation, message, fact and detail panel the header and the banner offer today stays available from the header, the message list or the body; each action reachable today without opening a menu is still reachable without opening one, except a message's own action and the journey-step and size control, which are one click away.

requirements.rationale: Open by default it took most of the list's column on the operator's project (14 changes, 72 defects).
requirements.statement: The spec list's defects report starts folded to one line showing the number of defects, and opens only when the operator opens it.

In roadmap order, in every list of specs, every change document that names a roadmap slice is listed under that roadmap, in the roadmap's slice order, whether or not the spec index records a parent for it.

requirements.rationale: Today approved and done are the same green dot. The operator chose set 2 (paperwork) on the mock, and asked that it apply wherever specs are listed.
requirements.statement: Wherever a spec's state is marked in a list of specs (the Spec tab's column, the side panel's Open a spec screen including its cards, its Specs switcher, and the search dialog), each state has its own icon (writing, ready, approved, building, done, capability, archived), done is a solid green disc with a check, and no two states share an icon.

requirements.rationale: The operator opens the list to find what is waiting on them; no other order answers that.
requirements.statement: Every list of specs offers a 'What needs you' order that groups documents as Waiting on you, In progress, Approved not started, Finished and Capabilities, and shows beside each waiting document why: ready to approve, amendments to review, ready to build, or ready to fold.

For every document it lists, the Hub returns the roadmap and slice the document names, if any, and which of these hold: being written with nothing blocking approval, amendments unreviewed or proposed, approved with open tasks and no build, done and not folded.
The shipped header and lists match the mock the operator approved, in the page and in the panel, in each state the mock shows.

in_scope: The spec document header and everything stacked between it and the body, in the page and in the side panel
The header condensing to one line while the body is scrolled

Every list of specs: the Spec tab's column, the side panel's Open a spec screen (cards and All specs), its Specs switcher, and the search dialog: footer, roadmap grouping by the document's named roadmap, state marks, and the 'What needs you' order
The Hub returning, per listed document, its named roadmap and slice and what it waits on the operator for

The panel's tabs, section chips, requirement strip and filter rows: they stay as they are (operator, 2026-11-02)
The wider side-panel rework (item 2 of the operator's 2026-10-28 note)
What any action, message or fact does or says
Writing a roadmap parent into the spec index
Grouping by product area: a change records its capability only once folded
Screens smaller than 1920x1080 as a target; they must still work

summary: The spec page gives its height back to the spec. The header becomes two rows, with every message behind one count beside the actions, and shrinks to one line once the body is scrolled. Every list of specs (the Spec tab, the side panel's Open a spec screen and switcher, and the search dialog) stops being pushed off screen by the defects report, groups slices under the roadmap they name, marks each state with its own icon so a finished spec cannot be mistaken for an approved one, and gains a "What needs you" order. Designed interactively with the operator on the mock (hub/ui/mock), and built from it.
